claim: ETH Zurich PACE pipeline trains quadrupedal locomotion policies for 30,000 PPO iterations using 4096 parallel environments and 24 steps per environment per update, yielding approximately 2.95 billion total environment steps per training run.
stance_target: Multi-billion-step training budgets are standard for quadrupedal locomotion PPO
scope_conditions: Quadrupedal locomotion (ANYmal, Tytan, Minimal); Isaac Gym/Lab; blind policy; no dynamics randomization
quoted_support: Number of iterations: 30,000. Steps per environment: 24. [with 4096 environments]

claim: The PACE framework performs parameter identification using CMA-ES on 4096 parallel simulated environments, converging within a range of computational time on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080.
stance_target: CMA-ES actuator identification is compute-efficient on a single consumer GPU
scope_conditions: Actuator parameter identification only (not policy training); CMA-ES optimization; RTX 3080
quoted_support: pace optimizations and simulations run on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080... With N=4096 environments, end-to-end optimization for each platform converges within [1 to] 24h per robot
numbers: 20 trajectories of in-air data per robot

claim: PACE eliminates the need for dynamics randomization in policy training by substituting accurate actuator parameter identification, and requires only 4 reward terms (vs. 10+ in prior SOTA locomotion work).
stance_target: Accurate physics modeling reduces training complexity and reward engineering burden
scope_conditions: Blind quadrupedal locomotion; PMSM-actuated robots; flat and rough terrain
quoted_support: Because pace identifies the dynamics end-to-end, we do not use dynamics randomization... Empirical evidence that only four reward terms suffice for effective locomotion training.

claim: PACE achieves a 32% reduction in Cost of Transport (CoT) for ANYmal compared to prior state-of-the-art, with ANYmal D reaching CoT = 1.27 versus ANYmal C at 1.86.
stance_target: Physics-grounded reward formulations outperform heuristic reward shaping for energy efficiency
scope_conditions: ANYmal quadruped; flat track locomotion; full Cost of Transport including electronics
quoted_support: achieving a 32 reduction in the full Cost of Transport of ANYmal (1.27)... CoT reduces to 1.27 (vs. 1.86 for ANYmal C)

claim: The PACE framework validates zero-shot policy transfer on 13+ legged robot platforms spanning humanoids, quadrupeds, and hexapods, demonstrating that the training approach generalizes across robot morphologies.
stance_target: PPO with physics-grounded reward trains generalizable locomotion controllers across diverse robot types
scope_conditions: 3 primary platforms + 10+ additional systems; open and closed-source platforms; PMSM-actuated
quoted_support: The framework is tested on three primary platforms and deployed on ten additional robots, demonstrating reliable policy transfer without randomization of dynamic parameters.
